issue: #4474 (board), from #4473: the TD head-to-head's remaining gap. Round A: a 15 ms beat lead. Round B (amendment, knob binary): an activation-only phase vote where the kicks are symmetric.

mechanism_evidence.latency: #4413/#4473: Fosfora's fired instants read +19 ms late vs the Harmonix holdout annotations (lastBeatStanding +4-6 ms); aligned F .700 vs raw .692. tools/bench_offset.py on the ship root's own dumps (main d7b175d, binary b50aa366): best constant lead Harmonix tune +15 ms (F .7528 -> .7599), Ballroom tune +10 ms (.5708 -> .5726, .5715 at 15); monotonic gains up to 20 ms on every half. The holdout curves were READ for this measurement before freezing (Harmonix holdout best +18 ms: .7114 -> .7185 at 15; Ballroom holdout +10: .5270 -> .5280 at 15) and are disclosed here; the holdout verdict below is still the single read of the arm's dumps.
mechanism_evidence.cook: at the next 60 fps frame (what a TouchDesigner consumer sees) the 15 ms lead forecasts Harmonix tune .7389 -> .7569, Ballroom tune .5682 -> .5729.
mechanism_evidence.mechanism: the locked grid's beat is EMITTED BEAT_LEAD_SECS = 0.015 before its instant on the mute state of the last settled instant; the instant settles (support, trim, mute, arbiter fold, sidecar) exactly as before. Checked on 4 holdout tracks: the beat sidecar is byte-identical to d7b175d, locked beats move by exactly -15 ms, acquisition fires by 0, beat counts identical except one beat at a mute transition on 2 of 4 tracks.

amendments.what: The first lead binary (8a19ca6aa9611bac, launched 15:30:19Z) fed the downbeat and structure trackers the EARLY beat pulse: their per-beat evidence windows ended 1-2 hops short and the downbeat placement changed outright (0770: 125 of 126 downbeats elsewhere, bar_phase held at 0 after each beat). That arm was killed unread and its root deleted. The replacement (02a469fa73ed2ad4) carries BeatResult.settled_beat_time: the trackers run on the instant's settle as before, /downbeat is stamped with the beat's emitted time. Verified on 4 holdout tracks: beat sidecar byte-identical to d7b175d; 0770 and 0958 identical except every locked beat and downbeat at exactly -15 ms; 0005 and 0618 differ by one beat at a mute transition (the early emission reads the mute state of the last settled instant) and the bar counters after it. Unit test scheduler_beat_times_strictly_monotonic_through_mode_churn failed on the first binary (an acquisition fire within 0.3 period of an early emission after a lost lock); the emission now records last_fired_time.

lead10 arm added on the tune read above (no holdout read yet): the exact per-track shift forecast on tune reads 10 ms Harmonix +.0062 (0 lost / 2 gained), Ballroom +.0018 (4 lost / 4 gained) vs 15 ms +.0071 (1 / 6) and +.0007 (6 / 8). Arm: the knob binary 8fde52e60b115136 with FOSFORA_BEAT_LEAD_MS=10, root q4474_lead10. Selection between lead10 and lead15 on TUNE: the higher harmonix + ballroom beat_f sum, ties within .002 to the fewer tracks lost; the chosen one is read once on the holdout. The frozen P3 is kept as written and will read MISS for both; the flip guard a shift can meet is lost <= gained per dataset, recorded here as the reading, not as a replacement target.

round_B.mechanism: Where the half-beat and quarter tests abstain, an activation-only fold over the 32-beat window votes the half-beat when its half bin holds act_ratio x its on bin with at least act_min activation events AND the kicks of the same window are symmetric (|on - half| <= kick_sym x (on + half)). Same streak (3) and offset as the half-beat rule.
round_B.population: tools/evidence_pop.py on the q4402 base sidecars (tune): Harmonix 8 T-level anti-phase grids, 4 with symmetric kicks of which the activation favors the beat on 2 (0599_boyfriend, 0954_timeaftertimevan); Ballroom 29 anti-phase, 11 symmetric, activation favors the beat on 4 (Media-100605, 103909, 105605, Latin_Jam4-01). Risk population (on-beat grids, symmetric kicks, activation favoring the half): 0 on both tune sets by the whole-track fold; the replica finds 2 Harmonix tracks (0673_feelsliketonight, 0558_allnightlong) whose events favor the off-beat in one section.
round_B.replica: tools/replay_q.py (replay_n.py + half_long_min / act_ratio / act_min / kick_sym), validate on the base sidecars 524 tracks 101,693 votes 0 mismatches; forecasts against the shipped quarters rule (--shipped q24r3), approximation as #4402's (the recorded grid's PLL).

selection.reason: No act arm passes the frozen set: both flip batida techno s8 (G3), act2s3 also loses 3 Ballroom tracks (P3). The combined lead+act arm therefore does not run and no holdout is read for round B. The activation-only vote is a recorded negative at these settings: on real music it trades Ballroom +.004-.007 against Harmonix flips (0673 .98 -> .51/.61), and on a synthetic exact-label techno render it moves a correct grid, which is the failure a visual rig would see. A later arm could raise act_min (12+) to keep breakdown-sparse windows from voting; not run in this round.

tune_result_lead15.reading: The live arm matches an exact per-track shift forecast (tools/shift_flips.py): Harmonix lost 1 / gained 6 at 15 ms = the forecast exactly; Ballroom forecast lost 6 / gained 8. The frozen P3 ('a pure shift loses none') was a false premise: a shift trades the tracks that sit at the 70 ms edge, both ways. Batida: the baseline's renders already read +17 to +29 ms LATE on synthetic exact-label kicks (house +20, lofi +18, rock +25, techno +19, waltz +29); the lead brings them to +3 to +14 and leaves their beat F flat, so the instants' lateness is the detector's, not an annotation convention.
